newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian markets expected stable in coming week.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian markets expected stable in coming week.

text.p: Indonesia's financial markets are expected to open relatively stable this week despite violence in the final days of the general election campaign last week, analysts said at the weekend.
They said the violence, culminating in the deaths of at least 134 people on Friday in the South Kalimantan provincial capital of Banjarmasin, had generally been factored into the market.

"I think the impact on the market will not be significant because violence in the run up to the election has been factored in," Pardi Kendy, treasury head of PT Bank Buana Indonesia, told Reuters on Sunday.
"Operators would be more scared if it (the Banjarmasin riot) had happened in Jakarta. We see the market here on Friday was relatively stable despite the widespread violence," he said.

The rupiah held its own against the U.S. dollar last week despite violence in Jakarta itself when many thousands of supporters of the Moslem-oriented minority United Development Party poured into the streets in confrontations with partisans of the ruling Golkar and security forces.
The rupiah last traded in Jakarta on Friday at 2,442.50 to the dollar against an opening of 2,441.
Brokers and analysts said sentiment on the stock market was likely to remain mixed ahead of the elections next Thursday.
"Bargain hunters are likely to keep their eye on blue chip counters," one broker said.
Jos Parengkuan, director of research at Lippo Securities, said there were bargains to be found.
"We think the market is relatively cheap and the economic fundamentals sound," he said.
But he added: "We're starting to see some disappointing corporate results and we're keeping our fingers crossed for the second quarter."
The composite index closed on Friday at 658.52 points, barely changed from 657.07 the previous week.
